commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Rewrite QDQ contractions into integer math

Rewrite contractions over affine-dequantized operands as integer
contractions with zero-point corrections and a scaling epilogue:

  C = sA*sB*(D - zB*RA - zA*RB + N*zA*zB)

Compose storage and parameter maps into contraction coordinates. Reduce
in integer arithmetic where parameters are invariant; retain the other
reduction dimensions as partial results for the floating-point epilogue.
Windowed operand sums use the same access expressions as the
contraction.

Match only plain multiply-add bodies with zero initialization. Require
positive static integer reduction extents and prove that all integer
intermediates fit in signed i32 using the separate storage and zero-
point ranges. Unsupported cases retain the original computation.

Apply corrections before converting to float. Evaluate scaling and
blockwise accumulation in at least f32, preserving wider scale and
output types, and narrow only the final result. Reassociation changes
rounding. Enable the rewrite by default; it can be disabled with
--iree-global-opt-enable-qdq-to-integer-math=false.

Cover the rewrite with three compiler regression files: correction terms
and widening, indexing maps and result shapes, and the contractions the
rewrite declines. Add CPU execution checks for blockwise and convolution
zero-point corrections alongside the original QDQ path.

commit_message:
[ukernel] Stop flushing bf16 subnormals in fp conversion

iree_uk_f32_to_bf16 flushed every f32 subnormal to zero, and
iree_uk_bf16_to_f32 did the same in reverse. That is right for f16,
whose smallest subnormal is 2^-24, but wrong for bf16: bf16 carries the
same 8-bit exponent as f32, so the subnormal ranges coincide and those
values are exactly representable.

iree_math_f32_to_bf16 in base/internal/math.h already handles this,
guarded on the destination having as many exponent bits as f32. The
ukernel copy exists because ukernels are freestanding and cannot include
base/, and it had drifted from it. Sweeping all 2^32 f32 inputs, the two
disagreed on 16711678 of them: every f32 subnormal that does not round
to zero, and nothing else.

Port that guarded branch into both directions of the ukernel conversion.
Narrowing needs a rounding shift of the mantissa, where a carry out of
the field lands in the exponent and is exactly how the largest f32
subnormals reach the smallest normal. Widening needs only a shift. After
this the two implementations agree on all 2^32 inputs.

f16 is unchanged, since the guard excludes it. Its own subnormal gap,
normal f32 values in [2^-24, 2^-14) that should become f16 subnormals
and currently become zero, needs renormalization rather than a shift and
is left for a separate change.

Both directions and the pre-existing normal path now share one
iree_uk_bias_to_nearest_even helper, mirroring how math.h factors the
same rounding bias.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>

[ukernel] Stop flushing bf16 subnormals in fp conversion

iree_uk_f32_to_bf16 flushed every f32 subnormal to zero, and
iree_uk_bf16_to_f32 did the same in reverse. That is right for f16,
whose smallest subnormal is 2^-24, but wrong for bf16: bf16 carries the
same 8-bit exponent as f32, so the subnormal ranges coincide and those
values are exactly representable.

iree_math_f32_to_bf16 in base/internal/math.h already handles this,
guarded on the destination having as many exponent bits as f32. The
ukernel copy exists because ukernels are freestanding and cannot include
base/, and it had drifted from it. Sweeping all 2^32 f32 inputs, the two
disagreed on 16711678 of them: every f32 subnormal that does not round
to zero, and nothing else.

Port that guarded branch into both directions of the ukernel conversion.
Narrowing needs a rounding shift of the mantissa, where a carry out of
the field lands in the exponent and is exactly how the largest f32
subnormals reach the smallest normal. Widening needs only a shift. After
this the two implementations agree on all 2^32 inputs.

f16 is unchanged, since the guard excludes it. Its own subnormal gap,
normal f32 values in [2^-24, 2^-14) that should become f16 subnormals
and currently become zero, needs renormalization rather than a shift and
is left for a separate change.

iree_uk_f32_to_bf16 flushed every f32 subnormal to zero, and
iree_uk_bf16_to_f32 did the same in reverse. That is right for f16,
whose smallest subnormal is 2^-24, but wrong for bf16: bf16 carries the
same 8-bit exponent as f32, so the subnormal ranges coincide and those
values are exactly representable.

iree_math_f32_to_bf16 in base/internal/math.h already handles this,
guarded on the destination having as many exponent bits as f32. The
ukernel copy exists because ukernels are freestanding and cannot include
base/, and it had drifted from it. Sweeping all 2^32 f32 inputs, the two
disagreed on 16711678 of them: every f32 subnormal that does not round
to zero, and nothing else.

Port that guarded branch into both directions of the ukernel conversion.
Narrowing needs a rounding shift of the mantissa, where a carry out of
the field lands in the exponent and is exactly how the largest f32
subnormals reach the smallest normal. Widening needs only a shift. After
this the two implementations agree on all 2^32 inputs.

f16 is unchanged, since the guard excludes it. Its own subnormal gap,
normal f32 values in [2^-24, 2^-14) that should become f16 subnormals
and currently become zero, needs renormalization rather than a shift and
is left for a separate change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
name: linux_x64_clang_byollvm

commit_message:
[ukernel] Stop flushing bf16 subnormals in fp conversion

iree_uk_f32_to_bf16 flushed every f32 subnormal to zero, and
iree_uk_bf16_to_f32 did the same in reverse. That is right for f16,
whose smallest subnormal is 2^-24, but wrong for bf16: bf16 carries the
same 8-bit exponent as f32, so the subnormal ranges coincide and those
values are exactly representable.

iree_math_f32_to_bf16 in base/internal/math.h already handles this,
guarded on the destination having as many exponent bits as f32. The
ukernel copy exists because ukernels are freestanding and cannot include
base/, and it had drifted from it. Sweeping all 2^32 f32 inputs, the two
disagreed on 16711678 of them: every f32 subnormal that does not round
to zero, and nothing else.

Port that guarded branch into both directions of the ukernel conversion.
Narrowing needs a rounding shift of the mantissa, where a carry out of
the field lands in the exponent and is exactly how the largest f32
subnormals reach the smallest normal. Widening needs only a shift. After
this the two implementations agree on all 2^32 inputs.

f16 is unchanged, since the guard excludes it. Its own subnormal gap,
normal f32 values in [2^-24, 2^-14) that should become f16 subnormals
and currently become zero, needs renormalization rather than a shift and
is left for a separate change.

Both directions and the pre-existing normal path now share one
iree_uk_bias_to_nearest_even helper, mirroring how math.h factors the
same rounding bias.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
